alternatives_rejected.why: The disk I/O deviation is the dominant signal (z~8.8e18 against a near-zero baseline, E1/E3). Heavy disk writes inflate page cache, which plausibly explains the +819% memory rise as a side effect rather than the cause (E3).
recommendationservice's own span self-time tripled (1.02->3.05ms) and inbound caller-observed latency rose 8.4x (E2), so the slowdown starts inside recommendationservice, not upstream of it.

proposed_fix.description: Identify the process or volume behind the abnormal disk I/O in the recommendationservice pod (for example with iotop or by checking for a runaway writer or stress job). First stop that writer or restart/reschedule the pod onto healthy storage; this interrupts service briefly but is recoverable. Then confirm that disk I/O and p90 latency return to baseline. Only after confirming what is filling the disk, and with operator approval, delete the offending temp files, since that step cannot be undone.
